{ "url": "https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets", "title": "Telegram Widgets", "family": "bot-api", "sha": "dfc14652a3a0a6e5b8405935a78f654abd956e0eb40cafcc33eacf7f2610919c", "checked_at": "2026-11-10T20:52:46.472228+00:00", "changed_at": "2026-11-10T17:50:04.877545+00:00", "error": null, "freshness": { "stale": false, "age_seconds": 542, "max_age_seconds": 21600, "refresh_error": null }, "body": "# Telegram Widgets Bots can send **widgets**: small interactive blocks drawn right inside a message. A widget is one self-contained HTML document with inline CSS and JavaScript, at most 32 KB of HTML and 4 KB after compression. Telegram apps run it on the user's device in a sandbox with **no network access at all**, draw it in the style of the chat, and keep it running while it is on screen: a poll whose bars move as people vote, a price ticker, a board game for two in a group, a promo code that copies on a tap. A widget is **fixed code plus changeable state**. The code, its HTML, is set when the widget is sent and never changes. What changes is the widget's state, and only the bot writes it: the **chat state**, tied to one message and seen only in that chat, and the **shared state**, seen wherever the widget is shown. The widget reads its state and redraws when it changes. It cannot change the state itself, but it can ask the bot with small requests, the way a callback button does. Widgets live in the private chat with the bot, in groups, in messages sent via the bot in inline mode, and in forwards to any chat. Currently, in the production environment, widgets work only in the private chat with the bot. The rest works on the [test server](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#availability). A widget can also be a **shared widget**: one widget on the server, like a poll, that any number of messages show, with one shared state for all of them. This page is a guide to designing and implementing widgets, followed by the reference of the widget's JavaScript object `TelegramWidget`. The Bot API methods and types for widgets are in the [Bot API reference](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api). --- ### Introducing widgets #### Code and state A widget is fixed code plus changeable state. * **The code** (the HTML with its CSS and JavaScript) is set when the widget is sent and never changes, in a message or in a shared widget. No method replaces it. For a new layout, send a new widget, and old messages keep the old one. As with any media, the caption can be edited. * **The state** is what changes, and only the bot writes it. There are two kinds: + **chat state** (`chat_data`): tied to one message, seen only in that chat (shared by all members in a group), never carried by a forward. A game in progress, whose turn it is. + **shared state** (`public_data`): seen wherever the widget is shown. A static widget keeps it in the message, and a forward gets a copy as of the moment of forwarding. A [shared widget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#static-and-shared-widgets) (one object with an identifier, like a poll) has one shared state for all its messages and forwards. Poll results, a price. * **The widget** reads its state, learns about changes through the `chatDataChanged` and `publicDataChanged` events, and cannot change its state itself: it can only ask the bot, with a [request](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#requests-to-the-bot). Details: [The widget's state](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#the-widgets-state). #### What a widget is * **One HTML document.** Inline `

item.text: В Bot API 10.4 есть метод `sendWidget`: он отправляет HTML с JavaScript прямо в личный чат. Для простого счётчика достаточно одного запроса — кнопка «+1» будет менять число на устройстве пользователя.

* Motion: transitions, `@keyframes` animations, timing functions (`cubic-bezier()`, `steps()`, `linear()`), `animation-play-state`, the animation and transition events.
* Values: `px`, `em`, `rem`, `%`, `ch`, `ex`, `vw` / `vmin` / `vmax` (the bubble's width), `calc()`, `min()`, `max()`, `clamp()`, custom properties and `var()`, `env(safe-area-inset-*)` ([the time in the corner](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#the-time-in-the-corner)), `content` with strings, `attr(data-*)` and counters.

* `touch-action: auto / pan-y / none`, `pointer-events`, `cursor`.

**Out:**

* `vh` and other height-relative units.
* `overflow: auto / scroll` (becomes `hidden`) and `position: sticky` (becomes `relative`).
* Logical properties (`margin-inline`, …), multi-column layout, `display: contents / flow-root / list-item`.
* 3D transforms and `perspective`, other filter functions (`grayscale()`, `saturate()`, …), `clip-path`, masks, blend modes.
* `text-shadow`, `-webkit-line-clamp`, `background-clip: text`, `writing-mode`.
* Modern color functions (`oklch()`, `color-mix()`, …).
* `env()` names other than the safe-area insets, and `url()` with anything but a `data:` image or a `#fragment`.
* `@font-face` and named fonts, `@import`, `@container`, `@layer`, `@property`, CSS nesting.
* `:has()`, `:focus*`, `::first-letter`, `::first-line`, `::marker`, `:target`, and form-state selectors (`:checked`, …). `:disabled` and `:enabled` work for `<button>`.
* `@media` on hover, pointer, resolution or print.

#### JavaScript

**In:**

* Layout reads answered by the app: `getBoundingClientRect`, `offsetWidth`, `getComputedStyle`, `matchMedia`, `elementFromPoint`, `ResizeObserver`. `IntersectionObserver` always reports visible.

* `attachShadow`, custom elements, `Blob`, `FileReader`, `URL.createObjectURL`, `requestFullscreen`.

* In canvas: `getImageData` / `putImageData`, `toDataURL`, `createPattern`, `createConicGradient`, shadows, `globalCompositeOperation`, `ctx.filter`.

* Touch events (use pointer events).
* Keyboard events and keyboard focus. There is no text input of any kind, and a key press never counts as a tap.

A forward, or another message showing the same shared widget, is another message, and its storage starts empty.\n\n**Links.** `openLink(url)` opens an `https:` URL of at most 256 characters (no user name or password, not a `t.me`, `telegram.me` or `telegram.dog` host) after the user confirms it, shown in full. `openTelegramLink(url)` opens a `https://t.me/…` link inside Telegram without a confirmation of its own, as a tapped `t.me` link in a message does (Telegram's own handling still confirms what it always does, such as joining a chat or a proxy). Both work only in the handler of a real tap, once per tap. A tapped `<a href=\"https://…\">` and `window.open(url)` do the same, through `openTelegramLink` for Telegram hosts and `openLink` otherwise. A URL these methods do not accept (not `https:`, too long, with a user name or password, a host of the other method, `tg:` links) throws `TypeError`. A tapped link or `window.open` with another scheme (`http:`, `javascript:`) is ignored.   "body": "#### Lifecycle\n\n* **Off screen** (scrolled away, the app in the background) a widget is paused: `document.hidden` is `true`, `visibilitychange` fires, `TelegramWidget.isActive` turns `false` with the `deactivated` event, animation frames stop and timers fire at most once per second. It resumes with `activated`.\n* **A widget can be destroyed and re-created at any time** (scrolled far away, memory pressure, app restart). Only the widget's state and Web Storage survive: redraw from them when the script starts.\n* `TelegramWidget.ready()` tells the app the first state is drawn. It is optional.\n* A widget that goes past one of its [limits](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#limits) (CPU, memory, nodes, text, operations, canvas, paint) or crashes is stopped: its last frame stays with a “Widget stopped” badge. The app rebuilds it when it is shown again. After two crashes in a row it stays stopped until the app restarts.\n\n---\n\n### What widgets support\n\nThe **widget profile** is the contract between widgets and Telegram apps: a feature is in when every app draws it the same way, and every app removes what is out before drawing. Something out of the profile never fails the widget: the declaration, selector, element or event is removed and the rest works. This page describes **profile 1**. A later profile only adds features.\n\n#### HTML\n\n**In:**\n\n* Text and structure: `div`, `span`, `p`, `br`, `hr`, headings `h1`–`h6`, `header`, `footer`, `main`, `nav`, `section`, `article`, `aside`, ",
